pr_title: Fix race condition in BatchBlock's handling of completion
pr_body:
When a BatchBlock is marked for completion, it will no longer consume postponed messages.  But the BatchesNeedProcessing method, which factors in the number of postponed messages, is accidentally ignoring the _decliningPermanently flag that indicates completion was requested.  As a result, with just the right sequence of operations, the BatchBlock can get stuck in a state where it sees postponed messages and queues a task to process them, but that task then sees that it's declining permanently and so doesn't touch any of the postponed messages, and then upon checking to see if it can complete, sees there are postponed messages, and loops again, resulting in a potentially infinite asynchronous loop.  The fix is just to check _decliningPermanently in BatchesNeedProcessing when considering postponed messages.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/38629
I've not yet come up with a good unit test for this, but prior to the fix I was able to hit the repro in the issue with some frequency, and I've not been able to trigger it after the fix.

cc: @tarekgh, @blushingpenguin

issue_context.title: System.Threading.Tasks.Dataflow gets stuck using 100% cpu waiting for block completion
issue_context.body:
### Description

I have created a minimal reproduction sample here:

https://github.com/blushingpenguin/DataflowHang

within a few seconds of running this (linux) or few minutes (Windows) then the dataflow will get stuck on "waiting for dataflow to complete" and spin the cpu (up to 4 cores worth, presumably matching the configured degree of parallelism for the blocks involved).

### Configuration

dotnet core 3.1.5
either ubuntu 18.04 x64 or Windows 10 x64

### Regression?

unknown
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.

Thanks for the repro.  I took a quick look, and I *think* the problem is that BatchBlock.BatchesNeedProcessing isn't factoring in _decliningPermanently.  _decliningPermanently is true, but BatchesNeedProcessing returns true rather than false; as a result, ProcessAsyncIfNecessary launches another task (which won't find anything to do) and then when it tries to complete the block, it finds there's a pending task (the one spawned by ProcessAsyncIfNecessary) and thus doesn't complete.  We just end up in this loop indefinitely.

I attached to a hung process, and it's definitely looping around spawning tasks in BatchBlockTargetCore.ProcessAsyncIfNecessary with _decliningPermanently = true.  In _nonGreedyState.PostPonedMessages, there is 1 message -- since the source has completed shouldn't this last message get forwarded though?  (I don't have a good handle on exactly what the code is doing so this could be totally off target though).

Thanks for looking at it so quickly!

> In _nonGreedyState.PostPonedMessages, there is 1 message -- since the source has completed shouldn't this last message get forwarded though?

No.  The repro has this code:
```
                fetchBlock.LinkTo(batchBlock, linkOptions, a => a != null);
                fetchBlock.LinkTo(DataflowBlock.NullTarget<JobThing>(), linkOptions);
```
That means that fetchBlock first offers the message to the batch block, assuming the message passes the filter.  If the message either doesn't pass the filter or if the batch block is full and postpones the message it was offered, the message will instead be offered to the next linked block, which in this case is a "null" target that will happily accept (and drop) everything.

But even if the source still had the message, if the batch block is marked for completion, that means it won't accept any more messages, which means it won't try to consume postponed messages.

> Thanks for looking at it so quickly!

👍
